bib.title: Agent Lumos: Unified and Modular Training for Open-Source Language Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Agent Lumos: Unified and Modular Training for Open-Source Language Agents. Da Yin, Faeze Brahman, Abhilasha Ravichander, Khyathi Chandu, Kai-Wei Chang, Yejin Choi, Bill Yuchen Lin. ACL 2024 Main (arXiv 2311.05657v3, Jul 2024). The note cites 2023 as the year (the first arXiv version).

COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages, 88,607 of 88,607 chars. I read the body, the limitations and appendices A-H in full. I skimmed the appendix I conversion-prompt examples, which are prompt text with no results, and the references. Extraction is clean. Two things were not extracted: the Table 1 cell layout was only partly legible, and the appendix prompts beyond I.1 and I.2 were not read.

Target note: I only read the note's header, not its body. It lists no Lumos URL in `sources:` (arXiv 2311.05657 is not among them). This source is SFT on converted rationales. It is not RL, so it fits the "SFT memorizes" thread or an agent-SFT-data example.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Splitting planning and grounding into two separately trained modules beats chain-of-thought training and a single integrated module.
  number: Lumos-I QA 65.7 / 45.9 vs Integrated 62.3 / 39.6 vs CoT 58.3 / 22.1 (StrategyQA / HotpotQA). Math GSM8K: Lumos-O 50.5, Integrated 45.5, CoT 40.4. Mind2Web: 27.6 vs 25.3.
  setup: LLaMA-2-7B, same base model and same data, 4 task types. CoT training was not run on web tasks. The gains on multimodal are small (A-OKVQA 71.3 vs 70.9; ScienceQA 58.4 vs 57.6). Lumos-O falls below Integrated on ScienceQA (56.9 vs 57.6) and on StrategyQA (60.6 vs 62.3).
  quote: "From Tab. 3, both LUMOS -I and LUMOS -O out-perform CoT Training3. They also exceed the integrated formulation based on a single module to operate planning and grounding. It highlights the importance of disentangling subgoal planning and action grounding skills during the agent training."
  where: p.7-8, §4.3, Table 3 (chars ~30000-34000)
- A 7B model fine-tuned this way beats GPT-4 on Mind2Web and GPT-3.5 agents on HotpotQA.
  number: Mind2Web step success rate 27.6 (7B) and 31.3 (13B) vs GPT-4 22.6 and GPT-3.5-turbo 15.7. HotpotQA LLM accuracy 45.9 vs ReAct 40.8 and ReWOO 42.4 (both GPT-3.5-turbo agents).
  setup: Mind2Web cross-domain test set, Lumos-I Web, which is trained on Mind2Web (starred in the table). HotpotQA uses GPT-3.5-turbo as the QA tool. HotpotQA and ScienceQA are held-out, with no fine-tuning on them.
  quote: "LUMOS -I de-livers superior performance by 5.0-8.7% over GPT-4 on Mind2Web. We also notice a 3.5-7.8% in-crease in LLM accuracy over the GPT-based Re-Woo on the HotpotQA dataset when employing GPT-3.5-turbo as the implementation of the QA tool to ensure fair comparisons."
  where: §4.2, p.6-7. Intro: "4.1% and 3.5% LLM accuracy improvement on HotpotQA over the ReAct and ReWOO agents".
- It beats open-source agents that are 2-10x larger.
  number: Mind2Web gains of 24.5% over WizardLM-30B and 14.1% over AgentLM-70B (7B Lumos-I). ScienceQA 67.3% vs AutoAct-7B 53.3%. SVAMP: Orca-Platypus-13B is 8.6% below Lumos-O.
  quote: "Specifically, 7B LUMOS -I achieves 24.5% and 14.1% step suc-cess rate improvements over WizardLM-30B and AgentLM-70B on Mind2Web."
  where: §4.2. The ScienceQA 67.3% is for the entire test set; Table 1c lists the IMG subset.
- Unified multi-task training generalizes to unseen tasks (WebShop, InterCodeSQL) with 2-3 shot examples in the module inputs.
  number: WebShop reward ~46-47 for Lumos-I (Web-13B 46.2, Math-13B 45.7, QA-13B 47.3; the All-13B WebShop reward is cut off in the extraction) vs Vicuna-v1.3-33B 23.9 and WizardLM-30B 10.6. Claim is "nearly 20 reward points". Lumos is 3-7 above domain-specific agents. InterCodeSQL success rate is low: All-13B 7.3, QA-13B 3.5, MM-13B 4.0, Vicuna-v1.3-33B 6.7.
  setup: few-shot examples are added in the module inputs, so this is not zero-shot. The first 500 WebShop instances were used. Claude-instant 49.7 and OpenChat-v3.2-13B 46.9 are about equal to or above Lumos.
  quote: "To makeLU-MOS adapt to these unseen tasks, we supplement 2-/3-shot examples in the module inputs" and "LUMOS -I achieves a 3-7 higher average reward than domain-specific agents on WebShop."
  where: §4.4, Table 1e, p.7-8.
- The training data are the ground-truth reasoning rationales of existing benchmarks, converted into a unified format by GPT-4. The method does not generate tasks from scratch.
  number: 55,382 planning and 55,499 grounding annotations (about 56K) after filtering. GPT-4 gets about 20% step success on Mind2Web, which is the stated reason for not generating annotations from scratch.
  quote: "Instead of creating annotations with LLMs from scratch, we exploit LLMs as a “style transfer” tool to convert ground-truth reasoning steps in existing benchmarks into the expected format in LUMOS formulations."
  where: §3 and §4.1.
- Better annotations beat the earlier Self-Instruct data (ReWOO-open), and high-level subgoals beat low-level ones.
  number: StrategyQA / HotpotQA 58.3 / 38.1 (Lumos data) vs about 57 / about 37 (ReWOO-open data). High-level subgoals 65.7 / 45.9 vs low-level 63.3 / 44.3.
  setup: 7B models, integrated formulation, 2,000 sampled training examples for the data comparison. The ReWOO-open numbers are approximate (≈) as printed.
  quote: "Note that even if the ReWOO-open data are based on HotpotQA, it still underperforms LUMOS on HotpotQA."
  where: §4.5, Table 2.
- Lumos-I (iterative, with execution feedback) beats Lumos-O (one pass) on QA but costs much more time. On math the two are close and Lumos-O is better.
  number: inference time for 100 instances, GSM8K 102s (O) vs 851s (I). HotpotQA 556s (O) vs 1007s (I). QA: Lumos-I 45.9 vs Lumos-O 39.2 (HotpotQA, GPT-3.5 tool). Math: Lumos-O 50.5 vs Lumos-I 47.1 (GSM8K).
  setup: 2 A6000 GPUs, batch size 16.
  quote: "LUMOS -O is a more efficient solution, but not as effective as LUMOS -I due to the lack of the adaptability to external environments."
  where: App. E, Table 6.
- Unified training across the four task types mostly helps and slightly hurts math.
  number: 13B, Web 31.3 to 31.9. QA 65.3/50.2/31.4 to 66.7/51.0/31.6. MM 72.4/58.2 to 72.8/58.2. Math held-in/held-out 51.9/66.3 to 50.5/65.8.
  quote: "The decline in performance for mathematical tasks is marginal, which is only 0.7% and 1.4%."
  where: App. F, Table 7. The quoted figures are as printed (they do not match the 1.4 and 0.5 gaps in the table).
- Mixing agent data with Alpaca instruction data keeps general instruction-following.
  number: 39.3 ROUGE-L vs 39.8 for LLaMA-2-7B on Alpaca alone (Super-NaturalInstructions).
  quote: "Lumos achieved a 39.3 ROUGE-L score, which is close to the LLAMA-2-7B trained on Alpaca alone (39.8)"
  where: §4.5.
- Training recipe and data scale.
  number: 2 epochs, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 128, max sequence length 1024, 3% linear warmup. Loss is computed only on assistant-response tokens. Data: math 19,778, QA 19,409, web 1,009, multimodal 17,056 source examples. Average turns per annotation: math 4.75, QA 3.75, web 8.25, multimodal 3.92.
  quote: "we implement training over two epochs with a learning rate of 2 × 10−5 and a batch size 128."
  where: App. D, App. B, §3.3.

LIMITS
- Authors concede three limits: only four training task types; no backtracking or replanning ("The current LUMOS lacks these sophisticated self-corrective features"); and QA experiments still use GPT models as tools, with an open-source replacement planned.
- The paper is SFT/imitation only, with no RL, reward signal or on-policy training. It makes no SFT-vs-RL comparison.
- The ground truth comes from GPT-4 conversion of benchmark rationales, so it is a distillation-like dependency on a closed model. Its quality depends on benchmark-provided rationales.
- Held-out claims are partly in-category. The "unseen" tasks need few-shot prompts. InterCodeSQL success is near 4-7%, which is low in absolute terms. GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 baselines on Mind2Web are taken from AgentBench numbers.
- Baselines are from 2023 (LLaMA-2, Vicuna, AgentLM, FireAct). The paper has dated, and no modern base model or RL-trained agent is compared.
- HotpotQA LLM accuracy uses a GPT-4 judge. QA evaluation uses samples: 300 StrategyQA, 1000 HotpotQA, three sampled sets.

BUILDS ON
- Task and agent formulations: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022b), Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023), SwiftSage (Lin et al., 2023), Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023), BOLAA (Liu et al., 2023c), HuggingGPT (Shen et al., 2023).
- Decoupled planning: ReWOO (Xu et al., 2023), with ReWOO-open as the data baseline.
- Agent fine-tuning: FireAct (Chen et al., 2023), AgentLM / AgentTuning (Zeng et al., 2023), AutoAct (Qiao et al., 2024).
- Data and distillation: Self-Instruct (Wang et al., 2023b), symbolic knowledge distillation (West et al., 2022), Distilling Step-by-Step (Hsieh et al., 2023), PlaSma (Brahman et al., 2023).
- Loss masking follows Wang et al. 2023a (How Far Can Camels Go).
- Evaluation settings follow AgentBench (Liu et al., 2023b) and ReWOO. Base models are LLaMA-2 (Touvron et al., 2023a). Source datasets include PRM800K, GSM8K, ASDiv, MuSiQue, StrategyQA, Mind2Web and A-OKVQA.

CODE (verbatim format snippets, App. A Fig. 3 and §2)
- Planning turn: "<|user|> Please provide a reasonable subgoal-based plan to solve the given task. Task: Who lives longer, Lowell Sherman or Jonathan Kaplan? <|assistant|> Subgoal 1 : Query the living period of Lowell Sherman."
- Execution feedback turn: "The execution result of Subgoal 1 is 46 years . Should we stop planning?"
- Grounding turn: "R1 = KnowledgeQuery(Lowell Sherman); R2 = ParagraphRetrieval(R1, Query: …); R3 = QA([R2], Query: …)"
- Loss (§3.3): L = − Pj log pπ(tj | t<j) × 1(tj ∈ Y), where the indicator masks user-prompt tokens.
- Formulations: S = πplan(T) for Lumos-O, and st = πplan(T, s1, e1, ..., st−1, et−1) for Lumos-I.

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.1): Lumos pitch, comparing it with closed-LLM controllers on affordability, transparency and reproducibility.
- Fig. 2 (p.2): the architecture. Planning, grounding and execution modules, with Lumos-O (one pass) side by side with Lumos-I (iterative). The worked examples are A-OKVQA and Mind2Web. This is the most useful figure.
- Fig. 3 (App. A): conversion from benchmark rationale to the planning and grounding chat annotations.
- Tables 1 (a-e), 3 and 7 hold the results listed above.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- Two-column extraction interleaves some text. Table 1e (unseen tasks) is truncated at the page break, so I could not read the All-13B WebShop reward or the full InterCodeSQL column.
- The App. F text says "0.7% and 1.4%" for the math decline, while Table 7 shows gaps of 1.4 and 0.5. I flag this as a source inconsistency.
- The paper has no RL content. Its relevance to the RL pillar is as an SFT-on-agent-trajectories data point, so the calling session should decide whether it belongs in this note.
